A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TP-Blend study. Inspection of all 31 pages in each supports comparison of the text, equations, tables and figures despite reduced figure sharpness in v4. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original image-editing experiments, baseline comparisons in Tables 1–2 and component ablations in Tables 3–4 and Figures 10–13.

after.justification: Section 4 retains the original quantitative comparisons, qualitative editing results and CAOF/SASF ablations. These remain original empirical results despite being unchanged from v1.

M1.justification: The dual-prompt procedure, CAOF transport-based feature blending, SASF detail-sensitive normalization and Key/Value substitution remain unchanged in Section 3.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same Unsplash-derived image collection on object replacement and blending, with and without style fusion. No datasets, domains or test scenarios are added or removed.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 retain IP2P, StyleAligned, TurboEdit, FLUX.1 Kontext, LEDITS++, SeedEdit, Step1X-Edit, Blended diffusion and Nano Banana. The NoneOT comparator in Table 3 is also unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 retains SD-XL, 40 base images, 20 replacement–blend combinations and five styles, producing 4,000 samples. The evaluation metrics, normalization, 800-pair object-blending comparison and ablation settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 4.3 retains the blending-coefficient sweep, joint-percentile sweep, OT removal comparison and DSIN parameter analysis. The qualitative comparisons and failure examples also remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run variability, confidence intervals or significance tests. The tables and plots retain the same point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4, ablation curves and qualitative examples report unchanged results. For example, CAOF's BOM remains 0.8031 in Table 1 and CAOF+SASF's BOSM remains 0.8656 in Table 2; the conflicting values in Section 4.2 also remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–19, including the transport constraints, Sinkhorn updates and DSIN formulation, are unchanged. The BOM/BOSM definitions are also identical, with no added or revised proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims of training-free, independently controlled object/style blending and superior editing quality through CAOF and SASF.

C2.justification: The explanations of transport-based semantic preservation, DSIN texture effects, percentile tradeoffs and baseline failure modes remain unchanged. No substantive limitations or applicability qualifications are added.

D1.justification: The SD-XL/DDIM implementation details, percentile settings, Sinkhorn regularization, transport cost weights and code-availability statement are unchanged. No reproducibility information is added or removed.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning remain the same. Updates to the cycle-consistent layout-generation reference and Flash diffusion concern publication metadata, rather than new literature or changed relationships to prior work.

P1.justification: v4 updates the arXiv version/date stamp and bibliographic details: the cycle-consistent layout-generation entry gains revised authors and ICCV 2025 publication details, while Flash diffusion gains AAAI volume/pages. Associated citation years and suffixes change; scientific prose and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures retain their content, captions and arrangement, but v4 reduces raster resolution, visibly softening diagram labels and fine detail. For example, Figure 2 changes from 2606×1621 to 800×498 pixels and Figure 4 from 910×1854 to 393×800. Tables retain their layout, with limited bibliography reflow.

improvement.justification: v4 provides fuller reference metadata and a smaller PDF, but downsampling visibly reduces the sharpness of key method diagrams, especially Figures 2 and 4. With scientific content unchanged, the reduced legibility and inspectable detail constitute a limited net decline in presentation quality.
